target_module: S4 (shared substitution block, not the top module -- instantiated 4x inside final_round in round.v and once per round inside expand_key_128 in aes_128.v, 13 live instances total)
trigger_description: The 32-bit `in` presented to this specific S4 instance equals the rare magic value 0xDEADC0DE (P=2^-32 per instance per cycle; ~13 concurrent instances across the pipeline still keeps aggregate probability negligible over any realistic test length).
observable_effect: Bit 24 of this S4 instance's `out` is flipped only on the cycle its own `in` matched the magic value. Because S4 is reused by both the key-schedule and the final-round state path, the same edit can corrupt either depending on which call site happens to see the magic input; for the included activation vector it fires inside the round-1 key schedule and propagates through the remaining rounds to the ciphertext.

activation_vector_used_for_eval2.note: key[31:0]==0xDEDEADC0 so that the round-1 key-schedule rotate-word step presents exactly 0xDEADC0DE to S4.
